So from what I can tell, the flow goes as such:

  1. Take the user to the authorization page. Have them either confirm or deny.

  2. Assuming the user clicked grant, receive access code

  3. Ask user for credentials again, send with access code. Receive auth token

  4. Send auth token with future requests.

Going off of this, I can't understand why I would need to ask the user for credentials twice. I'm trying to get around it with some javascript commands to reduce the number of steps, but it's quite messy. I want to be able to store the user's credentials on the system to ease future token refreshing, hence having them enter them into a box I can easily read.

Requesting more information about OAuth 2.0 on the api help page

You don't need to ask twice, you only need to ask once. However, the kind of authorization you are implementing (implicit grant type) does not allow you to store the user's credentials.

If you are making a javascript-based service, you won't be able to capture their login credentials. In your step 1, the authorization page you are redirecting users to will reside on Voat. When user enters credentials and clicks authorize/grant, your webservice will receive an access token (this is the oauth token). You are now able to immediately go to step 4 to make requests with this token.

In order to save/capture login credentials, you need to be implementing the Resource Owner Password Credentials Grant, which are for things like mobile apps and desktop applications. Here's a great website explaining different oauth2 processes.

I know I'm way too late on this, but what is your meditation practice like?
I currently don't have a routine. I've got some tapes and have been working with that, I also tried an AOL workshop at great expense to my wallet. Is there anything you'd recommend?

There are two basic things to work on in meditation: Pranayana and Asana. You don't need to pay any money to learn either. I'll give you the basics of what I know and do.

Pranayana- This is breathing. Basically, you regulate your breathing to focus the mind and change your thinking. What you wanna do is a Four Fold Breath. The technique is as follows: Breath in for a four count. Hold for a four count. Exhale for a four count. Hold for a four count. Repeat this cycle.

Asana- Asana is posture. Find one that works for you. What I do is sit in a straight backed chair, feet on the ground, hands on the knees. This is a fairly good posture, keeps the spine straight with the head fairly bent.

How do I actually meditate? Well that's the $10,000 question. You can't just do it whole hog. Start out and for about a week work on your posture. Start out with a small amount of time, say two minutes. Do that every day. If you fidget start over. This gives you a decent baseline.

Once you can sit in your posture for 2 minutes without fidgetting, what I want you to do is focus all your attention on a point. (the tip of your nose is the easiest) So now, instead of just sitting and not fidgetting, you're sitting and not fidgeting and focusing all your attention on your nose. Continue doing that until you just have that down.

Once you have that down, and you can do both those things for 2 minutes no problem, go for 5 minutes. Once you have it down for 5 go for 8. Once you have 8 minutes mastered go for 10.

Now add breathing. What you are gonna do is what's called the Four Fold Breath. Breath in for four, hold it in for four, exhale for four and hold that for four and repeat. As with the previous exercise, do that for 2 minutes starting out and as you get better increase it till you get up to 10 minutes.

Then you combine the posture, the breathing, and the focus and boom, you're meditating. I suggest mediating daily.

Once that's mastered you can do what is called discursive meditation. What you do in that is all the previous stuff, then when your mind is focused you switched to normal breathing and let your brain just run wild on a subject. It feels like you're having a conversation. Once you're done with that you fall into your breathing again for a little bit and then you're done.

There you go, a basic course on meditation and how to do it. I recommend once you get to the point where you're actually meditating that you do it daily. It helps calm the mind and makes you better at magic.
